summary: The lecture covers Part I (Articles 1-4) of the Indian Constitution dealing with the Union and its territory, including the integration of princely states, linguistic reorganisation of states, key constitutional provisions for state formation/alteration, and the evolution of Jammu & Kashmir's special status (Articles 370, 35A) and its 2019 abrogation.
points: Part I (Articles 1-4) defines India as a Union of States; territory comprises States, Union Territories, and acquired territories.
Article 2 empowers Parliament to admit new States; Article 3 allows formation/alteration of States by simple majority.
Article 4 clarifies laws under Articles 2-3 are not constitutional amendments under Article 368.
Madras State renamed Tamil Nadu on 14 January 1969 after Sankaralinganar's 75-day fast (27 Jul–13 Oct 1956).
Potti Sriramulu's 65-day fast (19 Oct–15 Dec 1952) led to Andhra Pradesh formation (1 Oct 1953) as first linguistic State.
Sardar Patel (with V.P. Menon) integrated 562 of 565 princely states; Junagadh, Hyderabad, Kashmir initially refused.
Article 370 (special status for J&K) added 17 Oct 1949 by Gopalaswami Ayyangar; Article 35A added 1954 by Presidential Order.
Both Articles 370 and 35A abrogated 5 Aug 2019 by Presidential Order under Article 370(3); J&K bifurcated 9 Aug 2019.
States Reorganisation Act 1956 (effective 1 Nov 1956) created 14 States and 6 UTs on linguistic basis per Fazl Ali Commission.
Goa became 25th State in 1987; Telangana (2014) is the latest State formed via Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act.

check.q: Which Article of the Constitution empowers Parliament to form a new State by separating territory from any State?
Who was the Chairman of the States Reorganisation Commission (Fazl Ali Commission) appointed in 1953?
On what date were Articles 370 and 35A abrogated by Presidential Order?
